title: Emergency Throttle Coordinator and Cross-Region Soft-Shed Orchestrator
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Background:
Redwood has multiple documented incidents where sudden traffic spikes (client-side retries, A/B tests, or transient downstream slowdowns) caused local token-bucket limiters to saturate in a single region, leading to either aggressive global failover to a single healthy region (increasing latency/cost) or complete request shedding for some customers. Existing limiter failover behavior is conservative: on limiter outage we default to coarse-grained shedding and lease transfers that are slow to converge.

Goal:
Design and implement an Emergency Throttle Coordinator (ETC) that: (1) provides bounded, auditable cross-region temporary credit sharing for short bursts, (2) orchestrates a deterministic soft-shed path with prioritized fairness, and (3) exposes observability and SLO hooks to tie degradation actions to SLO budgets and operator runbooks. The system must preserve per-customer fairness, be auditable for compliance, and gracefully degrade to strict per-region quotas when the coordinator is disabled.

Non-goals:
- Replacing long-term capacity autoscaling policies. ETC only targets sub-second-to-minute burst episodes.
- Solving client-side retry amplification; we will add client guidance and backoff policies separately.

Requirements & Acceptance Criteria:
- Safety: No single customer can exceed their committed quota by more than 10% while ETC is active.
- Convergence: After a transient (< 2 minutes) post-burst, allocations must converge back to normal per-region quotas without manual intervention.
- SLO integration: Actions (borrow, lend, soft-shed, hard-shed) must emit events linked to SLO budget usage and be visible on the Console SLO panel.
- Observability: Dashboards for current borrow pools, outstanding loans, per-tenant priority, and fallback counts.
- Auditability: All cross-region transfers produce signed, timestamped audit logs stored for 90 days.
- Rollout: Feature flagged per-tenant; default off for enterprise tenants until security review is complete.

High-level approach:
1) Coordinator concept: lightweight leaderless control-plane where region-local limiter instances advertise short-lived supply tokens to a global view (eventually consistent). A conservative bidding protocol matches needy regions to lenders.
2) Token economics: define three bucket classes: reserved (contracted), burst-eligible (short-term, rate-limited), and emergency-slush (strict cap, used only under circuit-breaker conditions).
3) Priority/fairness: each tenant has a dynamic priority score (usage velocity, historical fairness adjustments, SLO tier). Loans are awarded proportional to priority with hard caps.
4) Circuit-breaker integration: when underlying infra signals high tail latency or GPU OOM rates, the coordinator steps to soft-shed mode: it stops new loans and initiates proportionate request trimming using configured routes and hints from the Console rollout policies.
5) Deterministic drains: coordinator issues lease-drain tokens for in-flight borrowings to allow graceful KV-cache rehydration and prevents eviction storms.

Implementation notes:
- Protocol: use protobuf over the existing inter-region control plane (authentication via mutual TLS and signed tokens). Max message size small; only ephemeral deltas exchanged.
- Data model: store per-tenant outstanding loans with optimistic counters in Redis with TTLs and write-through audit entries to append-only store (S3) for compliance.
- Fallback: if coordinator is unreachable, region-local limiter reverts to algorithmic fallback: tight proportional fairness with pre-calculated emergency shares.

Testing strategy:
- Unit tests for bidding and priority math.
- Chaos simulations: run injector that simulates client spikes, regional packet loss, and replica lag. Measure convergence time and worst-case overcommit.
- Staging soak: enable feature-flag for 5 internal tenants across 3 regions for 2 weeks, monitor SLO panels and cost impact.

Rollout plan:
- Stage 0: Design review + security review (blocked until security sign-off).
- Stage 1: Internal-only flag, no cross-region lending in prod.
- Stage 2: Controlled pilot (5 tenants), read-only audit enabled.
- Stage 3: Wider opt-in for non-enterprise tenants.
- Stage 4: Enterprise opt-in post-compliance sign-off.

Open questions / trade-offs:
- Centralized leader vs leaderless matching: central leader simplifies global view but creates a single point of control. We propose a hybrid: leaderless bidding with ephemeral leader for tie-breaks.
- Storage cost of append-only audits vs queryability: currently using S3 + partitioned index; may need analytics copies for security team.
- Interaction with Dedicated capacity guarantees: ensure ETC never violates reserved capacity contracts.
